To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose three novel LSTM cell architecture variants, that jointly learn from two sequences, and that these architectures outperform state-of-the-art solutions in light field face recognition tasks.

the proposed novel LSTM cell architectures are able to create more effective description models by jointly learning from multiple 2D images rendered from a lightfield image or its descriptions, and that the proposed LSTM-based face recognition solutions, using these novel LSTM cell architectures as the core of their deep learning framework, achieve state-of-the-art recognition performance on the challenging LFFD dataset.

(1) the novel LSTM cell architecture with two input sequences, which jointly process them, outperforms the standard LSTM cell architecture with one input sequence; (2) the novel LSTM architecture, which processes a sequence of 2D face images, outperforms a state-of-the-art 3D CNN architecture; (3) the novel LSTM network, which jointly learns from two sequences of 2D images, outperformed the LSTM network, which learns separately from two sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a light field face recognition solution based on LSTM recurrent neural networks.

the development of novel LSTM cell architectures for deep learning networks, and their integration into a novel end-to-end deep face recognition solution, able to exploit the spatio-angular information of the light field images.
the design of new architectures for LSTM cell, which are able to create richer description models for visual data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, the proposed new LSTM cell architectures are able to create more accurate and richer description models, and therefore achieve better recognition performance, while being more efficient in terms of computational complexity, memory usage and parallelization ability.

, in terms of face recognition accuracy, the novel LSTM cell architecture solutions outperform the state of the art, with a gain of 1.8%, while in terms of memory and time efficiency they outperform the state-of-the-art solutions, by a factor of 1.7 and 3, respectively.
the novel proposed LSTM cell architectures are able to create richer description models for light field face recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we proposed three novel LSTM cell structures able to create richer models for visual recognition by jointly learning from sequences with specific dependencies between them.

, by using the proposed LSTM network architectures, we are able to achieve the state-of-the-art recognition performance on the challenging LFFD database, with a significantly reduced computational complexity, and a significantly lower memory consumption.

we proposed a new LSTM architecture, which is able to jointly learn from multiple sequences of images, which is more efficient and effective for visual recognition, and that we applied it to the challenging light field face recognition task.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the novel LSTM cell architecture is able to jointly learn from multiple sequences, and thus it can be applied to other computer vision tasks, where two sequences with some specific dependencies between them are to be processed.
the joint processing of two sequences with some specific dependency is a promising direction for the future design of LSTM cell architectures.

the novel LSTM cell architecture is able to jointly learn from the two sequences of rendered images, or their descriptions, and to exploit the spatio-angular dependency between them, thus creating more efficient and richer description models, which lead to better visual recognition performance.
